title: Grateful Dead Live at The Matrix on 1966-12-01
taper: 3 great sources of this music were provided by ANON to make this version, 2 were used Almost Certainly Recorded by Peter Abrams

ai_review.summary: Great‑sounding 1966 audience tape with hiss largely removed and a lively first set full of surf‑rock keys, bluesy harp and solid Garcia leads.
ai_review.review: The new remaster dramatically reduces the tape hiss that plagued earlier versions, though it sacrifices some high‑frequency sparkle. Musically the show is praised for its classic early‑Dead vibe – heavy organ, Pig’s bluesy harp work, Jerry’s lead guitar and a set packed with rarities like "Betty & Dupree" and "Cream Puff War." Overall the performance is viewed as energetic and representative of the band’s 1966 sound.

ai_rating.rationale: Strong musical impression with many positive comments, recording quality markedly improved but not perfect; rating reflects good show plus solid (though slightly lacking) audio.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hiss dramatically reduced in the new remaster; high‑end frequencies are thinner than on the original tape, but overall sound is clear and impressive for a 1966 audience source.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is a eclectic mix of 60s surf‑rock keyboards, Pig’s bluesy harp, and Garcia/Weir guitar work; the flow feels lively though some moments (e.g., Weir on "Minglewood") are noted as not quite hitting their stride.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s lead guitar is highlighted throughout, described as strong and central to the set.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh’s bass playing receives a positive nod, mentioned alongside the organ in driving the groove.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm work is noted ("hitting with Minglewood but not quite there"), indicating solid but uneven performance.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboards are described as heavy and surf‑rock oriented, with the organ/“Pig” presence dominating the early set.
